text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Latency regression detected in us-west-2 serving tier. p50 +120ms, p95 +680ms over baseline for the last 5m. Spike started ~4990012320. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/latency-4990012345

alex: seeing the same on the logs. p95 shifted on model-engine requests, not universal. Looks correlated with increased minor page faults and higher syscall wait times.

maria: any recent kernel or infra changes in that region?

alex: there was a maintenance kernel bump on ~4990012200 to 5.15.24 -> 5.15.28 on a subset of nodes (autoupdate). Rollout was ~10% of pool.

samir: sharing perf counters from an affected host (abbrev):
```
% cpu  sys  user  iowait
idle  48.2  6.8   44.0  3.6
softirq +25% vs baseline
page_faults/sec: 420 -> baseline 30
context_switches/sec: 12000 -> baseline 6000
```
Looks like stall on page reclaim.

lee: traces show tail spans in model-serve loop waiting on `page_fault` and `copy_from_user`. Example span: `kernel:page_fault_handler -> userspace:vnread` duration 180ms in the slow calls. Sharing trace: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/4990012345/abc123

maria: customer impact? any 5xx or timeouts?

alex: some timeouts, mostly 504s on long generation requests. Impacting ~3% of total requests in us-west-2 but 18% of long-running calls (>4s). Notified 2 enterprise customers (via status page).

oncall-bot: Current on-call: alex. Next on-call: samir (in 2 hours). Paging severity: Sev2.

alex: immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) divert long-running requests to fallback lighter model variant 2) add more capacity by spinning up spare dedicated nodes (fast) 3) isolate autopatched nodes and roll them back or reprovision.

maria: do (1) now — can we patch routing rule? I can update the routing policy to prefer fallback-model v2-fallback for requests with max_tokens>1024.

alex: go for it. Also start scaling up the dedicated pool by +30%.

samir: started a probe to drain one patched node and reprovision. Giving command runbook: `./infractl drain-node --region us-west-2 --node n-12345`

lee: attaching a small excerpt from dmesg that shows repeated soft pagefaults on affected node: `softirqs: __do_softirq+0x...` Noting a pattern around kernel memory reclaim.

alex: timeline so far: 4990012200 kernel rollouts begin (10%); 4990012320 latency uptick; 4990012345 alert fired; 4990012360 routing change applied (fallback model); 4990012400 scaled dedicated pool +30%; 4990012450 drained 1 patched node for reprovisioning.

maria: routing change live. p95 dropped ~200ms within 1m for long requests (partial). Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/compare/4990012345

samir: reprovisioning patched node now. If this is kernel regression, we should stop the rollout. Who controls the kernel rollout policy?

alex: infra team owns rollout; tagging infra@redwood. But we should pause the remaining rollout immediately.

lee: hypothesis list so far:
- H1: kernel memory reclaim change in 5.15.28 increases soft pagefault overhead -> raises p95 (most likely)
- H2: workload shift increased cache pressure uncovering bug in our mmap handling (possible)
- H3: unrelated user-space change coincident with kernel rollout (low confidence)
We need kernel perf counters and kernel tracepoints across patched vs unpatched hosts.

maria: collecting perf data and will upload to s3: s3://redwood-debug/4990012345/perf.tar.gz

alex: customer comms: posting to status page noting degraded performance and targeted mitigation in play. Not escalating to Sev1 yet.

oncall-bot: Handoff note: samir will take overnight on-call once alex signs off. Marking incident handoff channel for followups.

samir: I'll take it. Next steps for me: (a) compare perf counters patched vs unpatched, (b) pull kernel oops/dmesg across drained nodes, (c) coordinate with infra to pause kernel rollout. If we confirm regression, request hotfix or rollback.

lee: adding a short perf snippet request: `perf record -a -g -- sleep 60` on both hosts, and `perf script` -> share. Also enable `trace-cmd` for page_fault events.

maria: uploaded perf bundle and a short extract of vmstat/pss: https://s3.console.redwood/internal/4990012345/perf-extract.txt

alex: p50 is back near baseline after routing + scaling. p95 improved but not fully recovered (down from +680ms to +320ms). We'll keep mitigation active.

samir: infra confirmed rollout paused at 10% and no further kernel patches scheduled. They're investigating a kernel upstream change to page reclaim heuristics.

alex: ok wrapping up for now — leaving running tasks for samir. If you pick this up, annotate the timeline with new findings and update the hypothesis status.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded. Incident channel: #incidents/4990012345. Oncall: samir.

samir: acknowledged, taking over. I'll post an update within 30m with perf differential and suggested RCA next steps.

alex: thanks all. :thumbsup:
